# Tests {.unnumbered}

On this page we perform some tests:

- Check that equation macros render well in PDF and HTML (MathJax)
- Test some non-standard MathJax extensions
- Check that python runs well
- Check that a proper bibliography is generated
- Any other relevant test...

This page has to be commented in `_quarto.yml` for final production.

## Python code / graphic 

We test the Matplotlib style sheet `physrev_mplstyle` to be used to generate Physical Review compatible plots. We directly use the example provided on the style sheet repository.

See [https://github.com/hosilva/physrev_mplstyle/tree/main](https://github.com/hosilva/physrev_mplstyle/tree/main).

```{python}
#| label: fig-test_matplotlib
#| fig-cap: "A simple line plot generated with Matplotlib using `physrev.mplstyle` and `plt.rcParams` set to 150 dpi ."


import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


plt.style.use('../physrev.mplstyle')
plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = "150"

f, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1)

x = np.linspace(0, 1)
s = np.flip(np.arange(1, 1 + 9/10., 1/10))

for slope in s:
    ax.plot(x, slope * x, label="{:0.1f}".format(slope))

ax.set_xlim(0, 1);
ax.set_ylim(0, 2);

ax.set_xlabel(r'$x$')
ax.set_ylabel(r'$y = s \, x$')

ax.legend(ncol=3)
ax.get_legend().set_title(r"Values of $s$")  
ax.grid()

# For Mathematica default palette
# filename = 'example'

# For gnuplot default palette
# filename = 'example_gp'

# For README
# plt.savefig(filename + '.png', dpi=600) 

# For paper:
# plt.savefig(filename + '.pdf')
```


```{python}
#| label: fig-line-plot
#| fig-cap: "We create a second plot without specifiying the styles and size options."


x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
y = np.sin(x)

ax.set_xlabel(r'$x$')
ax.set_ylabel(r'$y =  \sin\left(x\right)$')

plt.plot(x, y)
plt.show()
```


```{python}
#| label: fig-line-plot3
#| fig-cap: "We change the size option to 200 dpi"

plt.rcParams['figure.dpi'] = "200"

x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
y = np.sin(x)

plt.plot(x, y)
plt.show()
```

We still need to work to fully understand the size options in quarto, especially in context of dual HTML and PDF output. But this is working for now...

## Some fancy equations structures

### Test 1: `eqnarray` without Markdown equation delimiters `$$ $$`

```{latex}
\begin{eqnarray}
a & = & b,\label{eq:f11}\\
c & = & d,\label{eq:f12}\\
e & = & f,\label{eq:f13}
\end{eqnarray}
```

\begin{eqnarray}
a & = & b,\label{eq:f11}\\
c & = & d,\label{eq:f12}\\
e & = & f,\label{eq:f13}
\end{eqnarray}

PDF: :white_check_mark: pass

HTML: :x: fail ()


### Test 2 : `eqnarray` with Markdown equation delimiters `$$ $$`

```{latex}
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
a & = & b,\label{eq:f11}\\
c & = & d,\label{eq:f12}\\
e & = & f.\label{eq:f13}
\end{eqnarray}
$$
```

$$
\begin{eqnarray}
a & = & b,\label{eq:f21}\\
c & = & d,\label{eq:f22}\\
e & = & f.\label{eq:f23}
\end{eqnarray}
$$

PDF: :white_check_mark: pass

HTML: :x: fail ()

### Test 3 : `eqnarray` with Markdown equation delimiters `$$ $$` and Quarto label `#eq-`

```{latex}
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
a & = & b,\\
c & = & d,\\
e & = & f.
\end{eqnarray}
$${#eq-eqnarray-global}
```

<!--
$$
\begin{eqnarray}
a & = & b,\\
c & = & d,\\
e & = & f.
\end{eqnarray}
$${#eq-eqnarray-global}

-->


PDF: :x: fail (compilation failure)

HTML: :white_check_mark: pass




### Test 4:  `aligned` with Markdown equation delimiters `$$ $$` and Quarto label `#eq-`

```{latex}
$$
\begin{aligned}
a & =  b,\\
c & =  d,\\
e & =  f.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-f3}
```


$$
\begin{aligned}
a & =  b,\\
c & =  d,\\
e & =  f.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-f3}


PDF: :white_check_mark: pass

HTML: :white_check_mark: pass


Seems to be the most robust, even though it does not allow numbering of individual equations, nor references to individual equations. At least it results in the same numbering in HTML and PDF formats.

See some [discussions](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/2275){target=_blank}.
